newsitem.title: USA: Calif. retail diesel prices rise, gasoline falls.
newsitem.headline: Calif. retail diesel prices rise, gasoline falls.

text.p: Retail diesel fuel prices in California edged up this week, as production eased from higher levels earlier this month, according to the California Energy Commission (CEC).
Gasoline prices went the other way for the opposite reason -- that is prices went down as production went up, the California agency said.
As of May 26, retail prices for state-mandated (CARB) gasoline averaged $1.34 a gallon, down one cent from a week earlier, amid higher production levels.
The average price of diesel fuel stood $1.31 cents gallon for the week period ending May 28, up one cent from a week earlier, the CEC said in a weekly survey of retail diesel prices.
"Right now, suppy and demand are more in balance. The inventories aren't as high as earlier in the month," said Claudia Chandler, a CEC official referring to diesel.
Production of CARB-grade diesel averaged 134,000 barrels-per-day last week, down from 182,000 bpd on May 2.
The highest diesel prices were in southern California, where fuel sold for $1.36 a gallon on average.
Northern California prices averaged $1.34 a gallon, while central Califorania stood $1.26 a gallon for the week.
On the gasoline front, CEC said average daily production of gasoline in the latter half has been around 937,000 barrels compared to 1.01 million barrels a day at the beginning of the month.
CEC did not provide regional breakdowns on gasoline prices, but plans to do so soon.
